boundaries.label: Presentation — binds the ViewModel, never the SDK, storage or network
domain + application — no QtGui, Widgets, Quick, Network or Sql
Adapters — the only layer that touches the SDK, storage or network
platform — per-OS code, consumed by the adapters

cards.title: One slice = one backend slice
items: slice folders are fixed: domain/ · application/ · adapters/{in,out}/ · presentation/{viewmodels,views}/ · contracts/
the same name appears in the folder, the URL module, the permission prefix, the realtime topic and the tests — a slice never imports another slice's internals
shared behaviour moves into shared-kernel or behind a port; composition happens once, in the composition root

cards.title: Ports, not imports
items: the consumer declares the port, the adapter implements it: SessionPort, SecretStorePort, RealtimePort, PolicyPort, ClockPort, NotifierPort, NavigatorPort, UpdaterPort
ports return QFuture<Result<T>> — errors are values, exceptions never cross a layer or a slot boundary
the ViewModel talks to use cases and to the Navigator/Notifier ports; it never holds a widget or a window pointer

cards.title: The CMake graph is the law
items: one target per layer and slice: domain_<slice>, application_<slice>, adapter_<slice>, viewmodel_<slice>, view_<slice>, plus platform and contracts
target_link_libraries lists only the allowed targets, so a layer violation fails at link time instead of in review
the composition root is a single app target that links the adapters and builds the ViewModels

cards.title: The walls CI enforces
items: domain and application do not include QtGui, Widgets, Quick, Network or Sql — the CMake link graph plus the clang-tidy include checks
#ifdef Q_OS_* appears only under platform/ — a grep gate in CI
views do not include the SDK, storage or network — the CMake target graph; a NOLINT without a reason is itself a review finding
